messages:
priya: Quick follow-up from the RFC: do we want bench suites defined per-model-variant or per-family? worried about N^2 combinations of quantization x batching x seqlen states.

alex: Short answer: perimeter gates at the family level, exhaustive perf matrices per-variant. Keep binary/behavioral checks extremely narrow and fast.

maria: Proposed flow to keep admits moving: 1) fast-binary check (<=20s) 2) light perf smoke (3-6m) to catch obvious regressions 3) exhaustive nightly bench across variants.

sanjay: For the light perf smoke, use relative baselines at family-level. initial thresholds: p95 <= 1.5x baseline, median <= 1.1x, throughput >= 90% baseline. If smoke fails, it goes to triage.

rachael: Add seqlen buckets: [16, 128, 1024]. Also do cold/warm passes to capture KV-cache stabilization (run 2 passes, compare second).

bench-bot: queued: light-perf-smoke run for family=opt, model=opt-1.3b, sha=sha1234

maria: Storage for golds: s3://redwood-onboard/gold/<family>/<model>/<sha>/gold.json and a meta.json with provenance. Keep gold corpus tiny (10-20 examples).

alex: Also plan to persist a small canonical trace for perf replay: s3://redwood-onboard/traces/<family>/<model>/<sha>.trace. Traces should be <1MB and deterministic-ish.

sanjay: Quarantine policy idea: any binary/behavioral fail => auto-quarantine. light-perf-smoke fail => move to triage queue with tag `perf_regression` and `smoke_failed`.

rachael: Triage playbook (sketch):
```text
- rerun light-perf on alternate infra (cheap-gpu vs reference-gpu)
- run deterministic ops-compat smoke (ABI/ops-only)
- collect perf traces + flamegraphs
- if flaky, escalate to eng-ml oncall
```

priya: Ops question: where should light-smoke run? prefer cheap-gpu or smallest supported infra so we catch quant/onnx/compat issues early; full bench runs on representative infra matrix overnight.

alex: Agree. Also add a gating key `deterministic` for ABI-only checks so they are idempotent and don't produce flakiness from concurrent infra noise.

maria: Publish an admit-metadata artifact on successful admit containing: baseline_sha, bench_hash, gold_sha, admit_timestamp, infra_key. This should be write-once (immutable).

sanjay: +1 on immutable admit-metadata. Also record the failing-run artifacts into a quarantine bucket with tags for triage.

rachael: I'll draft the RFC follow-up with YAML examples and an opt-in migration path for existing models. Tagging @eng-ml @eng-runtime :eyes: 

priya: Thanks — this gives me enough to iterate on the follow-up draft :thumbsup:
